title: It goes up on all four sides. Does it exist? (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The small staircase is where the hall does its counting: STEP moves a marker, FORM moves the return. Everything else on the floor is about what that counting does and does not settle.
hero.staging: The staircase stood 16 m from the arrival at the north edge and the other works in the corners against the columns; the pass brought them in (0bfd411f5). The model is straight ahead of the arrival with a ring under it, the pipe beside it, the beams and the trident either side, and behind it the door to the roof where the same stair is climbed.

plates.title: 1  I WANTED TO WALK IT BEFORE I KNEW IF IT COULD EXIST
front: A staircase that goes up on all four sides and comes back. I believed it at once.
Each corner I look at is a good corner. Each flight is a good flight.
My eye checks pieces and reports the whole. Nobody checked the whole.
So 'I can see it' was never evidence that it can be. It was evidence about four corners.
The wanting came first. Keep that: the wanting is not the mistake.
back: the hall says it shorter: the eye is already round the next corner, and the body would have to account for every step.

plates.title: 2  EVERY HEIGHT ADDED ONCE, TAKEN AWAY ONCE
front: Press STEP and watch the marker. Up, up, up - and one side gives it all back.
Why must it? Each move is one height minus another. Go all the way round and every height has been added once and taken away once.
The total is zero before I look at a single number.
That is not a fact about stairs. It is a fact about measuring every step against the same up.
A closed walk cannot end higher than itself.
back: the first proof on this tower I could redo in my head while standing. four heights a, b, c, d: (b-a)+(c-b)+(d-c)+(a-d).

plates.title: 3  YOU CAN MOVE THE RETURN. YOU CANNOT REMOVE IT
front: Press FORM. Five arrangements of one wish.
CLOSING DROP: fifteen steps rise and the sixteenth falls the whole way. The return, gathered into one place.
OPEN RUN and SCAFFOLD: no return - and no closed stair either. More scaffolding is not the missing step.
TILTED TREADS: the centres stay level and the eye climbs along the tilt. The instrument and the eye are answering different questions.
Hide it, gather it, cut it, tilt it. The return is still owed.
back: which one persuaded me first? the tilted one. I trusted the edges over the readout.

plates.title: 4  UNLESS YOU CHANGE THE AGREEMENT
front: The hall says it itself: a portal, a changed gravity or a moved room would be another agreement.
Behind this door I built that one. Every flight goes up and you come back to the door.
It cost this: twice a round you are set down 1.2 m and turned about, and so that you would not see it, everything in view had to be made the same from two places.
The return was not removed there either. It was paid outside the measurement - in the tablet's third line.
An impossible object is possible if you give up one honest thing. Say which.
back: what the body experienced on the way: nothing. that is the unsettling part, and it is the hall's own question.

plates.title: 5  WHERE YOU HAVE TO STAND
front: Three beams. From the green mark their ends meet. One step sideways: a gap.
Nothing in the beams moved. Two points far apart lay on one line from my eye.
The picture was true of that one place and false of every other.
A mark on the floor that says: believe from here. I am allowed to leave it.
What else do I only believe while I stay where I was put?
back: with two eyes the trick gives out sooner. one eye is a camera; two are already two places.

plates.title: 6  FOLLOW WHAT YOU COUNT
front: Two round rods at the base. Three flat tines at the top. I counted both and both counts are right.
Two becoming three is no crime. Branches do it.
The question is what I think I am following: one edge. Does it split, go behind, or turn into the edge of something else?
I cannot keep my finger on a single edge all the way. That is the whole impossibility: not the counts, the following.
A name on a sculpture does not settle it. Following does, or fails to.
back: the trident in this room is a solid thing, so it CAN be followed. it is the drawing of it that cannot. I am not sure this object shows the drawing's trouble or only names it.

plates.title: 7  RECOGNITION IS GENEROUS
front: A mesh, a frame, a sentence: this is not a pipe. I saw a pipe before I asked what I could do with it.
The engine draws it perfectly and it still cannot be smoked.
Recognition hands me stairs I want to climb and joins I expect to hold.
The hall does not ask me to stop. It asks me to walk up, count, move my head - and keep the pleasure.
Finding how it was made did not spoil the stair behind the door. I checked.
back: I am the generous one here too: I recognise an argument before I have followed it. this cardboard is me counting.

plates.title: 8  WHAT WOULD COUNT AS MAKING IT?
front: So does the endless stair exist? I made something. You can climb it.
But what I made is one lap and a rule for moving you. Is that the stair that goes up on all four sides?
Three answers on this floor. It cannot exist (the same up, a closed walk). It exists in the picture (from one place). It exists as a procedure (if you accept being moved).
The next room asks only for the third kind: show me how to make it, or do not say it is there.
First edge a choice, second a contradiction, third a reach. This one is about what 'there is' means.
back: Goedel, one floor up: true but not provable. here: seen but not buildable. the same gap? I do not think so - a picture is not a truth. not sure.

threads.why: Wanting it does not show it; counting the heights does.
If the total is zero the gain must come back somewhere; the five forms are where.
The return cannot be removed under one up; change the agreement and it is paid elsewhere.
I believed the stair as I believe the beams: from where I stood.
Leaving the mark breaks the beams; following an edge breaks the trident.
The following fails because recognition had already joined the edges for me.
Recognition supplied the stair I wanted to climb before I asked whether it could be.
A lap and a rule for moving a body: does that count as the stair?
The sum says it cannot exist; the next room will ask what a 'can' has to show.
From the mark it is there. That is one of the three answers.

visual_arguments.title: THE ROOF WHERE EVERYONE CLIMBS
visual_arguments.claim: The stair that goes up on all four sides can be climbed, if you give up one thing: being measured against the same up all the way round.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'A portal, a changed gravity or a moved room would require another agreement - and another question about what the body experienced on the way.' And the intent's named gap: an impossibility the learner undergoes.
built_from: a roof 160 m south of the tower: wide steps round a tower, a pavilion on every corner, drawn like a print by a shader
twelve robed walkers and eighty-eight small figures on the tower's walls
a sky of paper with hatched clouds in opposite pairs
visual_arguments.what_stands: A dark door frame behind the staircase model, with a board beside it.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Go in. Keep the tower on your left and climb. After four flights you are in the door's pavilion again; the tablet says how much was taken back.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: Every flight honest, every corner honest, and the whole closed only by moving the body. For that to go unseen, everything in view had to be made the same from two places.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/roof_stair_walk.gd, the tower's walker: tablets 1, 2, 3, 4, 1; 2.4 m climbed, 2.4 m taken back, 1 cm from where it stood; out by the door (6 of 6). Not tried in a headset.

visual_arguments.title: THE SAME STAIR IN A CARDBOARD BOX
visual_arguments.claim: The same rule needs no special world if the climber cannot see out.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: The same sentence about a moved room.
built_from: a closed cardboard stairwell round a block, 5 m square, with a ramp to its door
visual_arguments.what_stands: Nothing on this floor: its row was taken off when the roof was built (Palle: wider, more like the drawings, stranger). The work is registered and its probe passes.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: As on the roof. Its second setting, `kept`, keeps the hall's agreement: the stair ends 1.8 m above its door.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The kept setting is the hall's OPEN RUN at body size: four flights that only rise cannot close.

open: Plate 6: I am not sure the solid trident shows the trouble of the drawn one or only names it.
Plate 8: whether 'seen but not buildable' and 'true but not provable' are the same kind of gap is left open, and I lean no.
The roof is my own design in the manner of an impossible print; it copies no existing picture.

threads.why: The eye runs ahead corner by corner; the whole is nobody's check.
The descent had to be there: the sum round a closed walk is zero before any number is read.
Measured against one up, a closed walk cannot end higher.
Relocated, gathered, cut or tilted: the return is still owed.
Give up the same up - move the body - and the return is paid outside the measurement.
The roof pays it at the corners, where nothing in view records it.
Nothing moved but me: the meeting was true of where I stood.
Two points on one line from the eye: one image, two positions.
The mark is an offer. Leaving it is the test.
Recognition supplies the whole from the pieces.
Both counts are right; what fails is following one edge through.
Not in space under one up, not only in a picture: as something done to a body.
